predecessors.name: Ming dynasty
predecessors.text: the Jianzhou Jurchen country round Hetu Ala and the Hulun tribes (Hada, Hoifa, Ula) that Nurhaci had subdued before 1616

successors.name: Qing dynasty
successors.text: the whole Later Jin / Qing realm of 1642-1644, from which the Qing row of Cliopatria begins in 1645

rulers.name: Hong Taiji (Abahai)
rulers.title: Khan, then emperor of the Qing from 1636

ledger.x: 1616: Nurhaci declares himself Khan and founds the Jin (the Later Jin) at Hetu Ala.
1618: Nurhaci issues the Seven Grievances against the Ming and attacks in Liaodong.
1618: Fushun passes to the Jin.
1619: Tieling falls to Nurhaci.
1619: the Yehe, the last of the four Hulun tribes, are defeated.
May 1621: the Liaodong fighting ends in a Jin victory.
May 1621: Liaoyang and Shenyang pass to the Jin.
1622: the rest of Liaodong (the peninsula) is Jin land in Cliopatria's 1622 shape.
1622: the court moves from Hetu Ala to Tungking (Liaoyang).
April 1625: Shenyang becomes the capital.
February 1627: the Jin cross the frozen Yalu and invade Joseon.
1627: the Jin leave Korea.
1632: Hong Taiji and his Mongol allies march on Ligden Khan's Chahar.
1635: the Northern Yuan submit and the Chahar war ends.
1635: Inner Mongolia passes to the Jin.
1636: Hong Taiji renames the realm Great Qing (the Later Jin ends in name, not in state).
1636: Cliopatria draws all of Heilongjiang as Jin land from 1636.
1636: the first Amur expedition.
ledger.cp: Evenk and Daur tribes of the Amur

ledger.x: 9 December 1636: Hong Taiji invades Joseon.
28 January 1637: King Injo surrenders.
January 1637: Joseon becomes a Qing tributary.
1640: the battles for Songshan and Jinzhou begin.
1640: the Evenks are conquered.
ledger.cp: Evenk and Daur tribes of the Amur

ledger.x: 1640: the Amur region passes to the Jin.
1642: the battles for Songshan and Jinzhou end.
1642: Liaoxi (Jinzhou, Songshan) is Jin land in Cliopatria's 1642 shape.
1644: Cliopatria's 'Later Jin Dynasty' row ends and its 'Qing Dynasty' row begins in 1645.

wars.name: Nurhaci's conquest of Liaodong (Seven Grievances to Guangning)
wars.outcome: Jin victory: Fushun 1618, Tieling 1619, Liaoyang and Shenyang by May 1621, the Ming defeated at Guangning in 1622 with 16,000 killed.

wars.name: Ningyuan and the Yuan Chonghuan defences
wars.outcome: Ming defensive victories: Nurhaci was defeated at Ningyuan in January 1626, the Jurchens again in 1627, and Hong Taiji in 1628, all by Yuan Chonghuan; no border moved.

wars.name: Later Jin invasion of Joseon (1627)
wars.outcome: The Jin crossed the Yalu in February 1627 and left; the terms are not on the pages opened.

wars.name: Chahar campaigns against Ligden Khan
wars.outcome: Ligden fled in 1632 with perhaps 100,000 Chahar to Kokenuur (Qinghai), died of smallpox at Sira Tala in 1634 and his son Ejei Khan submitted to the Later Jin in 1635; Inner Mongolia passed to the Jin.

wars.name: Jin raids into Ming territory (Shanxi raids of 1632 and 1634)
Qing invasion of Joseon
wars.outcome: Qing victory: Injo surrendered on 28 January 1637 and Joseon became a Qing tributary, breaking with the Ming; no cession of land.

wars.name: Amur expeditions and the conquest of the Evenks
wars.outcome: Four major expeditions between 1636 and 1644; the Evenk conquest was completed in 1640 with the capture of Bombogor.

wars.name: Battles for Songshan and Jinzhou
wars.outcome: Jin (Qing) victory: the Later Jin page has Hong Taiji 'resoundingly' defeating the Ming 'in a series of battles from 1640 to 1642 for the territories of Songshan and Jinzhou'; Cliopatria draws Liaoxi as Qing land from 1642.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey bounds the Jin: the Ming frontier in Liaodong and Liaoxi moves with sieges, the Mongol and Amur frontiers are tribal and approximate.
